$doc: The size ratchet — docs/design/modularization-2026-08/plan.md §2. files = burn-down caps at each offender-s current eslint-counted size (shrink-only; regenerate with scripts/lint-ratchet.mjs --update). standing = permanent exceptions, each with a reason, hand-managed. TEST FILES are never listed here: they keep the blanket 800-line cap in eslint.config.mjs, because a suite's length tracks the surface it covers.

packages/shared/src/states.ts.reason: the FSM tables (TRANSITIONS + SUBTASK/SETUP variants) — one file decides transition legality, by design (plan §5). Raised 285 → 300 when task.reopen landed (#264): a table whose job is to hold transitions grows when the FSM gains one, and capping that would be capping the feature, not the file.

packages/control-api/src/handler/fsm.ts.reason: THE FSM boundary (plan §5): one file decides transition legality — table, subtask gate, reducer, gate mutators. Splitting it would mean two answers to `grep transition(`, which is the failure this round exists to prevent. Domain command branches leave it; the reducer never does. Raised 400 → 410 when routineAccept landed (2026-08-19): the routine's server-verified accept is a REDUCER — the states.ts precedent verbatim: a file whose job is to hold the reducers grows when the FSM gains one, and capping that caps the feature.

apps/desktop/src/main/devsmoke/smoke-syn.reason: The --smoke-sync gate: a linear FSM narrative whose phases share state (ids, timings, the live db) and run top to bottom. The shot modes split into ten files because they are INDEPENDENT; these are not, and threading a wide phase context through a dev harness would cost more clarity than it buys. Dev-only and lazily imported, so it never reaches a shipped build. Phase-splitting stays open if it grows.

packages/control-api/src/store/memory.ts.reason: The in-memory Store: 162 methods that must behave EXACTLY as PostgresStore does. Cutting it into repositories is plan §5's C-store-4, gated on a shared contract suite — today's memory/pg test pairs are hand-written twice with mostly disjoint cases, so nothing proves the two agree. Splitting first would let them drift silently, which is the one failure this layer cannot afford.

apps/desktop/src/renderer/preview/mock-f.reason: The preview harness's fixture WORLD: rows for every surface a shot can capture (rooms, tasks, threads, runs, skills, marketing, footprint). It is data, not behaviour — splitting it by domain would scatter one coherent fixture set across files that must stay mutually consistent, and the bridge that reads it is now its own module. Revisit if behaviour creeps in.

apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/brain/Brai.reason: The brain pill and its two tabs. The pill LABELS ITSELF from both tabs' state — the roles cast and the active pack — so a roles/packs split does not divide the state, it lifts about twenty values into props and leaves the pill reading all of them anyway. Exit condition: split the moment the pill's label stops depending on the tabs (a derived summary on the row, or the popover owning its own label), which is the only change that makes the seam real.

packages/control-api/src/commands.ts.reason: The command union. The plan's open question — does splitting members across modules keep zod's per-member inference — is ANSWERED: a spike spreading `as const` tuples from two modules into z.discriminatedUnion kept both `Extract<Command, {type}>` and per-branch narrowing (the spike's @ts-expect-error on a foreign field still fired). So the split is safe and worth doing. It is NOT done here because a member scanner was twice fooled by quotes inside comments, and a silently dropped schema means the server rejects a valid command. Exit condition: split by domain with an assertion that the set of z.literal names is identical before and after — the same guard that caught three lost tools in the orchestrator registry.

packages/control-api/src/app.ts.reason: The HTTP surface. Route ORDER is load-bearing — `use /v1/*` gates everything below it, and the file says so at the line that matters. Splitting routes across modules makes that order an emergent property of import order, which is the failure this file already documents. Exit condition: none expected; extract only leaf helpers. · 2026-08-31: 700→707 for the credit-pack checkout route + the webhook's pack-grant branch (credits round); both compressed to the minimum readable first. · 2026-08-31 (money-path fix): 707→710. The webhook's grant branch has to distinguish three outcomes now — granted, ledger unavailable, grant failed — because answering Stripe 2xx on a failure meant a charged customer with no credits and no redelivery. The logic itself LEFT this file (applyCreditPack in credits.ts, the leaf-helper extraction this entry prescribes, -8 lines); what remains is the three-line mapping from outcome to status, and collapsing it to a nested ternary would obscure the one branch that must never be wrong. · 2026-09-05 (desktop Code bridge, rule D9): 710→712. /v1/messages learns the two birth facts of a session — threadMachineId and threadOrigin — as one schema line and one field line; the origin is stamped `routine` for a schedule's post here because the API is the one place that knows a scheduleId posted it.

apps/desktop/src/main/agents.ts.reason: THE DAEMON'S ASSEMBLY. Down from 10,502. What remains is ~1,169 lines of module-level helpers and a startAgentHost that is now almost entirely wiring — makers, watches, timers, in the order boot needs them. Seventeen subsystems already left (host/*.ts). apps/desktop/src/main/sync.ts.reason: THE REPLICA'S BOOT. 52 inline IPC handlers became 10 across seven sync/ipc/ modules; what is left is the boot sequence — connect, resolve the workspace, register the machine, arm the reconnector — which is linear and ordered and must READ that way. Moving a registration past a boot await is how a whole watch layer silently never attached, with 823 tests green. EXIT: none proposed. A boot sequence is a script, and a script is meant to be read top to bottom.
